original_value: The centralized cooperative spectrum sensing (CSS) allows unlicensed users to share their local sensing observations with the fusion center (FC) for sensing the licensed user spectrum. Although collaboration leads to better sensing, malicious user (MU) participation in CSS results in performance degradation. The proposed technique is based on Kullback Leibler Divergence (KLD) algorithm for mitigating the MUs attack in CSS. The secondary users (SUs) inform FC about the primary user (PU) spectrum availability by sending received energy statistics. Unlike the previous KLD algorithm where the individual SU sensing information is utilized for measuring the KLD, in this work MUs are identified and separated based on the individual SU decision and the average sensing statistics received from all other users. The proposed KLD assigns lower weights to the sensing information of MUs, while the normal SUs information receives higher weights. The proposed method has been tested in the presence of always yes, always no, opposite, and random opposite MUs. Simulations confirm that the proposed KLD scheme has surpassed the existing soft combination schemes in estimating the PU activity.

result.paraphrase: Centralized cooperative spectrum sensing (CSS) enables unlicensed users to send their local sensing results to the fusion center (FC) for licensed-user spectrum sensing. While cooperation improves sensing, the participation of malicious users (MUs) degrades performance. The proposed method uses a Kullback Leibler Divergence (KLD) algorithm to reduce MU attacks in CSS. Secondary users (SUs) report received energy statistics to the FC so it can determine primary user (PU) spectrum availability. Unlike earlier KLD approaches that use each SU’s sensing information to compute KLD, this work identifies and separates MUs using each SU’s decision together with the average sensing statistics from all other users. The proposed KLD gives lower weights to MU sensing data, while assigning higher weights to normal SU information. The method was evaluated against always yes, always no, opposite, and random opposite MUs. Simulations show that the proposed KLD scheme outperforms existing soft combination schemes in estimating PU activity.
